transcript:
Meeting header - 2026-10-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO - Spectral), Marco Ruiz (Head Infra), Aisha Khan (ML Engineer), Tom Baird (Procurement)

Summary: Short discovery focused on p95 and streaming throughput targets for Spectral AI's chat assistant. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency guarantees, data residency, and cost. Agreed to run a benchmark harness with representative prompts; Redwood to propose pilot pricing and capacity commit options.

Topics covered: p95 SLOs, concurrency and burst shaping, streaming first-token vs full-stream latency, caching/KV prefix behavior, quantization and model variants, security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and pilot scoping.

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining we, um, appreciate you taking the time. quick round of intros - we'll keep this practical.
[00:12] Lena: hi yeah lena here cto, i'll kick it off - the core ask is predictable p95 for our chat surface, and we need to understand tradeoffs between hosted hosted, dedicated, and private deploys.
[00:23] Marco: marco - infra, i'll be the ops lead on the eval and want to be sure we can hit throughput targets without weird tail latency.
[00:30] Jordan: great, priya and i will go through how teams typically approach this. priya are you on audio?
[00:36] Priya: yeah i'm here - se at redwood. we'll try to map your traffic shape to config recommendations and then propose a pilot.
[00:43] Aisha: aisha - ml, i'll be sending prompts and we'll run some early tests. we have some sensitive data patterns so VPC or private is likely.
[00:52] Tom: tom from procurement - interested in how pricing changes for reserved vs bursty use.
[00:58] Jordan: perfect. so can you paint the workload - p95 target, typical prompt lengths, concurrency?
[01:06] Lena: target p95 ideally under 350ms first token for short prompts - think under 128 tokens. our median user session generates about 60 tokens, but we also have longer summaries up to 800 tokens for agent follow-ups.
[01:22] Marco: concurrency wise we see steady 150 concurrent active chats, with bursts to 600 during peak marketing pushes. we'd like a plan that handles bursts without dropping to a much higher p95.
[01:33] Priya: ok that's helpful - so short prompt first-token p95 of 350ms is in the ballpark for dedicated capacity on a tuned model, but in hosted tiers the numbers vary by model and multi-tenant noise. also streaming behavior changes measurement - do you care about first byte or full response latency?
[01:50] Lena: first byte is the most important for UX. we stream tokens to the client so first-token latency is our metric for p95.
[01:58] Jordan: noted - priya can you explain typical levers we use to hit that p95?
[02:03] Priya: sure - you have a few axes: reserved GPUs (dedicated) which gives predictable scheduling, smart batching and burst lanes for short requests, prefix/k-v cache to avoid re-computation on common system prompts, and quantized model variants to reduce per-token compute. also kernel selection and sequence-length aware routing matter.
[02:25] Aisha: about kv cache - we've seen mixed results. sometimes the transcriptions say k-v cask or something and i'm like what is that, haha. but yes repeated context should be cached.
[02:36] Jordan: yeah transcription is rough sometimes. on caching - we can keep session-level KV to avoid regen for common system prefixes. that reduces compute and first-token time a lot for short prompts.
[02:47] Marco: what's the expected tokens/sec per GPU for the model sizes we might use - we're likely to pick a 13B-ish open model tuned for safety.
[02:56] Priya: rough ballpark: with 13B and int8 quantization on modern A100/Infer-class hw you might see 80-120 tokens/sec per GPU for generation throughput. for streaming-first-token p95 it's more about scheduling and batch size - with continuous batching configured for low-latency you can get first-token times ~200-350ms depending on load. multi-tenant hosted will add jitter.
[03:18] Lena: ok so to sustain 150 steady concurrent streaming sessions at say 20 tokens/sec each that's 3000 tokens/sec sustained. by those numbers that's around 25-40 GPUs? is that right math?
[03:29] Priya: quick math yes, but a couple of notes - continuous batching helps consolidate tiny requests, KV cache will drop some compute, and you can use a mix of smaller models for quick replies and larger ones for long form. Also dedicated pools and burst autoscale behave differently - dedicated gives predictable latency but you pay for reserved capacity.
[03:49] Marco: for bursts to 600 concurrent, how do we avoid huge p95 spikes?
[03:55] Priya: options: pre-warm burst capacity, configured burst lanes that tolerate lower QoS for cheaper variants, and graceful degradation like falling back to a smaller model or truncated responses. Redwood supports routing policies - region/fallback/model-variant - you could keep a reserve of cheaper instances to absorb bursts.
[04:13] Jordan: i want to call out the private deployment constraints - if you're going private/on-prem we can run the same runtime but you manage the infra and network. that's preferred for sensitive data but it changes our ability to autoscale quickly.
[04:25] Lena: yes data residency too - we need EU only for portions of our traffic. can that be accommodated in hosted?
[04:31] Priya: yes hosted EU regions exist, and Dedicated can be region pinned. for Private we can deploy into your VPC or on-prem as part of the enterprise package. there are different audit and KMS options for each.
[04:44] Tom: procurement question - how does pricing differ between committed dedicated vs pay-as-you-go hosted?
[04:50] Jordan: committed reserved capacity has a lower per-token cost and predictable monthly bill. hosted is usage-based and good for early proofs. we'll include pricing tiers in the follow up.
[04:58] Aisha: on benchmarks, we prefer to run a token/sec harness that mimics our traffic shape - priya do you provide that harness or do we bring our own?
[05:06] Priya: we provide a harness and can run it jointly; typical flow is you share the prompt set and token profile, we run both hosted and a dedicated-config benchmark and share p95, median, and tail metrics including first-token streaming.
[05:18] Marco: how long should the benchmark run? our ops likes to see at least 1 hour for steady-state and a shorter spike run for bursts.
[05:25] Priya: agreed - 1 hour steady-state plus 10-15 minute burst scenarios is our standard. we'll capture token/sec, p50/p95/p99, and CPU/GPU utilization.
[05:35] Lena: security - SOC2, SSO, SAML, and KMS/HSM info please. we also need audit logs and ability to redact or TTL logs.
[05:44] Jordan: yes we'll send the security pack. redwood's enterprise offering includes SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integration, audit logs retention settings. private/on-prem gives you full control of keys.
[05:54] Marco: one more thing - can you explain prefix caching more concretely? our system prompt is heavy and repeated per session. would that be cached so it doesn't get recomputed each call?
[06:03] Priya: yes ideally you push the system prompt into the KV cache or use prefix caching. when the session uses the same system prompt the runtime keeps the cached KV so first-token compute is just decoding. there are size/time tradeoffs for cache TTLs.
[06:18] Aisha: for quality - if we quantize to int8 does generation quality degrade noticeably? we've got a narrow safety bar.
[06:26] Priya: there's some quality delta, but we often recommend mixed-beta approach: int8 for lower-cost fast paths and fp16 for critical or long-form responses. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles by workload.
[06:38] Jordan: any competitors you're looking at?
[06:41] Lena: we've talked to a couple - anthropic and openai and some infra vendors. cost and tail latency are major differentiators.
[06:49] Tom: procurement wants clear SLAs for p95 - do you offer SLA credits if p95 isn't met?
[06:55] Jordan: for dedicated and enterprise contracts we have SLOs and credits; hosted has standard uptime SLAs but we can extend for committed customers. we'll put that in the doc.
[07:04] Marco: can we try a small pilot - maybe 4 GPUs reserved for a week and run a baseline against our prompts?
[07:10] Priya: yes that's a common approach - short pilot with reserved nodes to validate p95 and posture. we can scope a week or two and include runbook for the benchmark.
[07:18] Aisha: timeline wise we want to decide by end of month - roughly two weeks to run pilots and validate.
[07:24] Jordan: sounds doable. i'll draft pilot options and pricing.
[07:28] Priya: i'll prepare the harness and a runbook - we'll need your prompt set and traffic shape.
[07:33] Lena: i'll gather prompts and share by friday; also want a note on EU-only routing.
[07:38] Tom: and i'll wait for pricing to start our procurement cycle.
[07:42] Jordan: cool, quick recap and next steps - jordan will send pilot pricing, priya will send harness and proposed benchmark schedule, aisha will share prompts. we'll aim to run the benchmark week of 10-19.
[07:55] Marco: one more small note - instrument latency on client to ensure we measure frontend to first token. networking can add 50-100ms so we want to baseline that.
[08:05] Priya: good point - we'll include guidance for client-side measurement and recommended tracing hooks.
[08:11] Lena: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[08:14] Jordan: thanks all - we'll follow up with the pack and calendar invites.

End of call

Notes on transcript quality: some words were auto-transcribed incorrectly - eg k-v cache became k-v cask, dedicated was sometimes 'dedicate', and a few proper names were garbled. The team confirmed these in chat during call.

Referenced artifacts and links: - benchmark harness (to be shared by Redwood) - pilot pricing template (to be sent by Jordan) - security pack (SOC2, SSO, KMS notes)
